sourceIssues.correction: Use the local Cartier index of K_X + S at P, rather than the index of K_X. This is the log index of the localized plt surface pair; it gives the denominator of the different and kills local Weil divisor classes.
sourceIssues.reason: Over k = F_7, take X = Spec k[x,y,z]/(xy-z²), S = V(x,z), and P the vertex. The two resolution charts (u,uv²,uv) and (st²,s,st), in coordinates (x,y,z), are crepant and have one exceptional (-2)-curve E. Thus K_X is Cartier. The strict transform S′ meets E once, and f*S=S′+E/2; the snc pullback S′+E/2 proves that (X,S) is plt. Since div(x)=2S and (x,z) needs two generators at P, S is not Cartier. Adjunction gives different P/2. Hence the printed m=1 fails, whereas index(K_X+S)=2 works. More generally, for the plt surface chain with determinant d, the different coefficient is 1-1/d and d annihilates local divisor classes, forcing the log index to equal d. This is the surface adjunction calculation, not a claim about the canonical index. Lemma 4.2 only needs the standard-coefficient different.

sourceIssues.correction: For the version needed in Proposition 2.15, fix a finite set I ⊂ [0,1), require coeff(B) ⊂ I, and formulate both the bound of m distinct exceptional log discrepancies and the conclusion on the minimal resolution of the surface germ. The printed statement says minimal log resolution; the source proof and this repair concern the minimal resolution. No finiteness theorem for all discrepancies on all higher models is asserted.
sourceIssues.reason: On the A1 surface over F_7, put B=bC for the ruling C=V(x,z) and rational 0<b<1/2. Its one-curve minimal resolution is also a log resolution of this pair, and K_{S′}+bC′+(b/2)E=f*(K_S+bC). Thus the exceptional discrepancy is -b/2 (log discrepancy 1-b/2), varying infinitely even for b=1/n, n≥3. The snc model is 1/2-lc. There is one exceptional value, so m=1 under the exceptional convention; if strict boundary components are counted, the uniform bound m=2 still disproves the statement. For the repaired minimal-resolution version, write T=f^{-1}_*B and a_i for exceptional log discrepancies. Minimality and negativity give 0≤1-a_i. Adjunction gives T.C_i=2r_i+a_i C_i²-Σ_{j≠i}(1-a_j)C_j.C_i<2r_i≤8. With finite I these nonnegative sums of integer multiples of positive elements of I lie in a finite set. Together with the source’s bounded intersection coefficients, convexity and compression of constant runs on the at-most-three-legged graph, only finitely many bounded-size linear systems remain. Negative definiteness gives uniqueness. The fixed boundary of a flip sequence supplies I, so this repair addresses the cited use in Proposition 2.15. Merely bounding arbitrary real right-hand sides would not prove finiteness.

sourceIssues.locator: Published version, Lemma6.6 pp.28–29 and global Q-factorial clause of Corollary6.7(1) p.29
sourceIssues.correction: Conclude that the divisor is Q-Cartier on a neighbourhood of the special fibre. For a global conclusion, add properness over the DVR; the same repair is needed for the unrestricted Q-factoriality assertion in Corollary 6.7(1). sourceIssues.reason: Let R=Z_p, p>5, and let T be Spec R[x,y,z,w]/(xy-zw) with only its closed special vertex removed. It is integral, flat, normal and excellent. The special fibre is the punctured threefold node, hence smooth, S3, terminal and Q-factorial. The remaining generic vertex Z is closed in T and disjoint from that fibre, so codim(Z∩X,X)≥3. The ruling D=V(x,z) is Cartier on T\Z, restricts to a Cartier divisor on X, and does not contain X. Over K=Frac(R), use the small resolution xt=zs, wt=ys in N×P¹. On its charts z=ux,y=uw and x=vz,w=vy, with v=1/u, the strict transform of D has equations x and z. Since z=ux, its divisor line bundle restricts to O_{P¹}(-1) on the exceptional fibre. There is no exceptional divisor, so any Cartier multiple mD would pull back to that strict-transform multiple and also restrict trivially to the fibre, contradicting degree -m. Thus both stated global conclusions fail. dFH11 Proposition 3.1 explicitly retains a neighbourhood of the Cartier fibre. Under properness the closed complement of the Q-Cartier locus of a fixed D has closed image in Spec R; if it misses the closed point, it must be empty. The projective lifts in Theorem 6.1 have this properness. This example does not refute its other conclusions.

sourceIssues.correction: Choose Q-Cartier representatives with 𝒜|_X ≡ A and ℋ|_X ≡ H; clear denominators when constructing sections. For large m choose a primitive section of a divisible multiple of mℋ+𝒜, giving an effective 𝒟 that omits X and has 𝒟|_X ≡ mH+A. This repairs the claimed literal lifts and the effective perturbation construction. The subsequent application of the lifted-step argument to the perturbed boundary must still be justified; this correction does not claim to prove the whole of (2b).
sourceIssues.reason: Theorem 6.1 defines N¹ as Pic⊗Q modulo numerical equivalence. Its surjectivity supplies rational numerical classes, not specified line bundles or integral representatives of prescribed classes. The proof of (2a), p.31, correctly uses ≡; p.33 uses literal equality. The needed construction can be made numerically: H is nef and big on X, hence its lift is nef and big on the generic fibre; choose m so mℋ+𝒜 is generically big. For a sufficiently divisible multiple L, the nonzero finite torsion-free R-module H⁰(𝒳,L) has a primitive section. The kernel of restriction to X is πH⁰(𝒳,L), so the primitive section does not vanish identically on X. Its divisor restricts with the desired numerical class and is negative on the chosen ray because H.Σ=0 and A.Σ<0. The fixed-resolution hypothesis permits a sufficiently small boundary coefficient. These steps require neither completeness nor H²(X,O_X)=0. They do not by themselves identify the prescribed special flop or prove numerical descent after the perturbed step; those are separate proof obligations. The finding is retained as a local proof gap, not a counterexample to the theorem.
